basis.note: Topics from FE Chemical area 8, read in full. Objectives and their order are ours and follow the usual textbook sequence; unit 1 is assumed by the spec rather than listed.

big_ideas.title: In minus out plus generation equals accumulation
big_ideas.text: Every problem is this one sentence applied to a chosen boundary and a chosen quantity. Mass and energy are conserved; moles of a species are not when it reacts.

big_ideas.title: The boundary is a choice
big_ideas.text: A box around the whole process hides the recycle; a box around the mixing point exposes it. Picking the boundary that cuts the fewest unknowns is most of the work.

big_ideas.title: Pick a basis and count unknowns before solving
big_ideas.text: Flows scale freely until one is fixed. Degrees of freedom say whether the problem can be solved before any algebra is done.

practices.title: Set up
practices.text: Draw the boundary, choose a basis, name the unknowns and count the independent equations.

practices.title: Solve
practices.text: Write the balances and solve for the unknown, carrying units.

practices.title: Judge
practices.text: Say which balance or boundary to use and whether an answer is physically sensible.

los.do: Convert between mass fractions and mole fractions, and find the average molar mass of a mixture.
ek: Take 100 g or 1 mol as a basis; the average molar mass is the mole-fraction-weighted mean.

los.do: Convert a volumetric flow of a liquid or an ideal gas to a molar flow.
ek: Liquid: density then molar mass. Gas: n = PV/RT, with T in kelvin.

los.do: Solve a mixer, a separator and an evaporator with a total balance and one component balance.
ek: Two independent balances for two components; a component that passes through unchanged is a tie.

los.do: Count degrees of freedom and say whether a balance problem is specified.
ek: Unknowns minus independent equations: zero is solvable, positive is underspecified, negative overspecified.

los.do: Balance a mixing point to find a recycle flow, and explain what recycle, bypass and purge are for.
ek: The overall balance never contains the recycle stream; a purge stops an inert accumulating.

los.do: Identify the limiting reactant and compute percent excess.
ek: Divide each feed by its coefficient; excess is measured against the stoichiometric requirement.

los.do: Use conversion or the extent of reaction to find every outlet flow.
ek: n_i = n_i0 + ν_i ξ; one measured species fixes ξ.

los.do: Apply selectivity and yield to parallel reactions.
ek: Conversion says how much reacted; selectivity says where it went.

los.do: Relate single-pass conversion, overall conversion and recycle flow for a reactor with recycle.
ek: With complete recycle of unreacted feed the reactor feed is the fresh feed divided by the single-pass conversion.

los.do: Find the theoretical air for a fuel and the dry flue-gas composition at a given excess air.
ek: O2 needed per mole CxHyOz: x + y/4 − z/2. Dry basis leaves the water out; excess O2 and all the N2 pass through.

los.do: Compute a heat duty from sensible and latent heat, and the steam needed to supply it.
ek: Q = m cp ΔT for a temperature change, m ΔHvap for a phase change; add the steps along the path.

los.do: Find the outlet temperature of an adiabatic mixer.
ek: Enthalpy in equals enthalpy out; with one cp the outlet is the mass-weighted mean temperature.

los.do: Compute a standard heat of reaction from heats of formation.
ek: Σ ν ΔHf, products positive and reactants negative; elements are zero; the phase of water matters.

los.do: Find the time to fill or drain a tank at constant flows.
ek: dV/dt = in − out; with constant flows the level changes linearly.

los.do: Model the washout of a stirred tank and use its time constant.
ek: V dC/dt = −qC gives C = C0 e^(−t/τ), τ = V/q: 37% after one τ, 5% after three.

los.do: Find the time to heat a batch at a constant heating rate.
ek: m cp dT/dt = Q; with no losses the temperature rises linearly.
